MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 12, 2022
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Bucknum
at 5:00 p.m., on April 12, 2022, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on April 7, 2022, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9:
  (1 case).

PUBLIC COMMENTS (taken out of order)

Dave Smer, M.V.: Voiced concerns over the excessive speed of automobiles on Muirlands and the
lack of police presence. He stated that damage to a block wall on the corner of Muirlands and
Spartan has been damages for over a year and asked when this would be fixed.

City Council Minutes  1  March 22, 2022
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four City Council Members present and Mayor Pro Tem
Sachs absent.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced there was no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Vector Control Update

  Received report from Bob Ruesch.

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Expressed his disappointment on the District Map chosen and laid out his
concerns regarding the two-year term extension of Goodell and Kelley.

Michael Schlesinger, M.V.: Announced that the City was served with a summons and complaint
that he filed to challenge the City’s refusal to call the election for seats of Brian Goodell and Trish
Kelley. He pointed out his reasons for the lawsuit.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: She made an appeal to Brian Goodell and Trish Kelley to stand for election
this year and not extend their terms for two years. Questioned the terms and asked what is to stop
Council Members in the future to extend their terms.

Ed Maurer, M.V.: Spoke on Community Choice Energy and reference other Cities in Orange
County that are participating in these programs and encouraged the Council to do the same.

Helen Maurer, M.V.: Expressed her anger at the Council for not considering Community Choice
Energy. Spoke about climate change and voiced her concerns.

Mary Wathen, M.V.: Stated that she attended the Planning & Transportation Commission Meeting
and expressed that it was a terrific sight of the community standing together and encouraged the
Council to accept the recommendation of the Commission and vote no on May 10 to deny the zone
change for proposed Garden Plaza Development.

Gideon Victor, M.V.: He stated he agrees with the Commission’s decision to deny the zone change
of the Garden Plaza. He encouraged the Council to still look at mixed-use in other areas of the City.
He explained that mixed-use is very profitable for cities.
City Council Minutes  2  March 22, 2022
 Carlos Pianelli, M.V.: Commented that his Stop the Monster campaign is non-political and does
support sensible planning. He pointed out various developments throughout the City that do not
affect the traffic and outlined the importance of small businesses in our community.

Anita Goldin, M.V.: Thanked the Council for listening over the past few weeks regarding the traffic
and environmental impacts of the Garden Plaza re-zone. Expressed concern on the condition of the
Garden Plaza and asked if the City had any interest in buying the property. She asked that the
Council vote no on May 10 for the re-zoning of the plaza.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned why the City Attorney interject himself with the public when the
City Council should be responding. She stated that the City Attorney is protecting and controlling
the official narrative and feels he is misinterpreted her comments and taken her statements out of
context. She questioned if public resources through the City Attorney are being used to protect and
promote Council seats and to aid in re-election campaigns.

Michele Mitchell, M.V.: Thanked the Council and Staff for their great relationship with the Mission
Viejo Nadadores and all the hard work the City Council does for the community.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Sachs

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 22, 2022, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated March 11, 2021 in the Amount of $3,028,134.97

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated March 18, 2022 in the Amount of $586,988.71

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 25, 2022 in the Amount of $808,799.36

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  March 22, 2022
 5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2022

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February
  2022

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for February 2022

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for February 2022

  Received and filed.

9.  Los Alisos Boulevard, Marguerite Parkway, and Santa Margarita Parkway Pavement
  Rehabilitation (CIP 22837)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

10. Catalytic Converter Theft Ordinance

  Adopted Ordinance 22-344 Adding Section 11.25 to Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Establishing Regulations Prohibiting the unlawful Possession of Catalytic Converters
  in the City.

11. Dive Well Bleachers at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex

  (1) Approve the Conditional Agreement (A22-13) for a Cash-Gift Contribution to the City of
  Mission Viejo for public improvements to the Marguerite Aquatics Complex Nadadores
  Foundation as Grantor, and (2) issue a purchase order in an amount not to exceed $125,175
  to Southern Bleacher Company for the purchase and installation of new bleachers at the dive
  well.

12. Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Field Lighting (CIP 331)

City Council Minutes  4  March 22, 2022
   Approved the Plans and Specifications and authorize staff to advertise for bids for CIP 331 -
  Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Field Lighting.

13. Painting and Related Services at City Facilities

  (1) Approved the first amendment for Signature Painting (A22-14A) for Painting and related
  services at City Facilities; and (2) authorized a change order to the existing purchase order for
  Signature Painting in an amount not to exceed $90,000.00.

14. Air Conditioning Repairs and Related Services at City Facilities

  (1) Approved the second amendment for Control Air Enterprises, LLC for air conditioning
  repairs and related services at City Facilities; and (2) authorize a change order to the existing
  purchase order for Control Air LLC in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.

15. Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning Repairs and Related Services at City
  Facilities

  (1) Approved the second amendment for South Coast Mechanical for HVAC repairs and
  related services at City Facilities; and (2) authorized a change order to the existing purchase
  order for South Coast Mechanical in an amount not to exceed $130,000.00.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

16. Transportation Corridor Agencies (TCA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley.

17. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Goodell.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

City Manager Wilberg announced that on Thursday May 12 the City will be holding a Town Hall
Meeting on Sober Living Homes headed by Senator Pat Bates.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

City Council Minutes  5  March 22, 2022
 Council Member Goodell announced he will not be able to attend the next meeting. He also gave
a shout-out to Animal Services for assisting when his dog was attacked by a coyote.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated that she attended the Saddleback Valley Unified School District
Unified Games event on April 7 at Trabuco Hills High School. She also attended the Orange County
Business Council dinner along with Council Member Goodell and Mayor Bucknum. Council
Member Kelley announced on Saturday April 16 Lake Mission Viejo will be hosting Marine Lake
Day for the City’s Adopted Marine Battalion.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that every Tuesday morning at 8:00 a.m. at the Norma P.
Community Center the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce meets and he encouraged small
business owners to network. He also shared on April 21 at the Animal Services Center they will be
holding a five-city mixer. Lastly, he stated that on June 9 the Mayor will be hosting a State of the
City breakfast at the Arroyo Trabuco Golf Course.

Mayor Bucknum

19. Support an End to Both the State of California and County of Orange COVID-19 State
  of Emergency and Calling Upon the California Legislature to Revoke the Governor’s
  Emergency Powers

  Mayor Bucknum presented her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 22-07 Requesting and Supporting an End to the COVID-19 State of Emergency
  and Calling Upon the California Legislature to Revoke the Governor's Emergency Powers
  and the Board of Supervisors of the County of Orange to Rescind and Terminate the County
  Declaration of Emergency.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Raths
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Sachs

Mayor Bucknum stated that she has received outreach from residents regarding “street vendors” on
city sidewalks. City Attorney explained that the City is very limited due to SB946 which gives the
vendors protection. Mayor Bucknum clarified that the vendors have to allow a four-foot clearance
on the public sidewalk and asked staff to put a news article on the City’s website. She announced
that she along with Elaine Lister gave a presentation on Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU) and how
it relates to Home Owner Associations. She would like to do some outreach to the HOA’s and asked
staff to look into holding round tables with Board Members. She stated that the Council has been
huge advocates for the City regarding housing and the State and we are facing some political back
City Council Minutes  6  March 22, 2022
 lash as a result and she want the resident to know that it is election season and there will be legal
issues the Council will not be able to comment. Mayor Bucknum said that this Council are people
of integrity, we serve, and it is disappointing to see the division within our State for which she is
disappointed and sad. Lastly, she announced that she will be running for re-election and wished
everyone a Happy Easter, Happy Ramadan, and a very Happy Healthy Passover.

ADJOURNMENT AT 7:28 P.M. TO TUESDAY, APRIL 26, 2022, AT 5:00 P.M.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 26, 2022

City Council Minutes  7  March 22, 2022
